patterns.key_values: portrait utility settings window ~299px wide; segmented Picker (Format/Style/General) switching panes over an inset-grouped card of label+trailing-switch rows (~52px tall, faint left-inset hairline dividers); ~20px shared content inset; native capsule switches, blue-on/gray-off; accent reserved to switch state

WYSIWYG preview card atop the controls — a live desktop-thumbnail render of the corner-clock overlay (label bottom-left, live time top-right, r~12) sitting directly above the toggles that configure it; changes reflect in the preview

the shipped product is a background clock utility (fullscreen / hidden-menu-bar corner overlay) configured via this small settings window; runtime surface is chromeless SF Pro text mimicking the system menu-bar clock

signature_moves: Live WYSIWYG preview card directly above the toggles: renders the actual corner clock on the actual wallpaper so an ephemeral, off-to-one-side overlay becomes tangible while you configure it — the description-experience gap answered in the layout, the one decision that lifts a stock settings pane into something owned

The product disappears into the OS: runtime output is chromeless SF Pro white text typeset to pass as the native menu-bar clock, so a third-party overlay reads as a system feature (Jakob's Law working for the app) — the app's best design choice is to have almost no visible design
defects: Contrast Dilution (mild) — row-divider hairlines + off-switch track borderline <3:1 against the dark blue window; conventional for macOS grouped lists, a half-step lighter divider clears it

Non-real chrome state (render artifact, not an app defect) — lit-red + 2 gray traffic lights is a state macOS never produces; confirms the window is a stylized marketing render, so all control metrics are (estimated) at unknowable scale

Segmented-control-as-tab-bar (minor) — Format/Style/General does pane navigation, which HIG assigns to an in-window tab view ('a segmented control is not a tab bar'); accepted SwiftUI Picker idiom for small settings windows, a pattern quibble not a violation

aesthetic.direction: Platform-default SwiftUI settings chrome — no committed aesthetic direction beyond faithful macOS convention; the character lives in one component (the live preview card) and in restraint, not in a chosen range-map family. Closest map anchor is Neo-grotesque-product only insofar as it simply IS the system.

psychology: Description-experience gap / demonstrate-don't-describe (Hertwig & Erev) — the live preview card shows the actual overlay outcome instead of describing it; strongest possible answer for a feature you can't see while configuring
Jakob's Law (used correctly) — standard switches, segmented control, grouped list; and the overlay mimics the real menu-bar clock so the whole product reads as a familiar system feature
Feedback / Doherty Threshold — WYSIWYG design implies immediate apply: toggle -> preview updates, tightening the input->result loop
Hick's Law + progressive disclosure — ~4 toggles per pane, split across Format/Style/General so each decision point stays small
Von Restorff / accent restraint — blue reserved to the 'on' switches only; everything else neutral, so state is pre-attentively scannable
Aesthetic-usability effect (Kurosu & Kashimura) — clean, faithful native chrome buys first-contact trust for a background utility
notes: Single asset: a 1200x630 OG marketing composite, so three layers were separated per the cover rule and never conflated — the left app window (primary evidence), the top-right corner overlay (the product's real runtime output, a legitimate second surface), and the brand wallpaper/headline/wordmark. UNLIKE most single-cover digests in this corpus (Bauhaus Clock, Alcove — single-element renders), Corner Time's window shows a full, real settings pane with segmented control + grouped switch list, so this is a richer native-settings-pattern contribution. The window is a stylized render (red+gray+gray traffic lights prove it), so all metrics are (estimated) at ~1:1 pt scale (cluster ~60px vs native 68pt). Era called big-sur under dark-mode humility (Liquid Glass unconfirmable in a dark still). App icon (icon.png, a white Big Sur squircle with a black header bar showing '09:41' over a blank silver panel — the corner-clock-as-display-widget conceit) was NOT digested: task scope is Workflow A (UI) only; flagged here for a future Workflow B pass. Contributes to a menu-bar-utility config-pane cluster; the live-preview-card signature is worth watching for recurrence across other overlay/config utilities (Alcove, notch tools) toward canon.
